queries.q: In the 2011 NIST cloud definition, how many essential characteristics, service models, and deployment models are there?

span.text:
This cloud model is composed of five essential characteristics, three service models, and four deployment
models.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: This cloud model is composed of five essential characteristics, three service models, and four deployment models.

queries.q: How much location control does the customer normally have when a cloud provider pools resources?

span.text:
There is a sense of location
independence in that the customer generally has no control or knowledge over the exact
location of the provided resources but may be able to specify location at a higher level of
abstraction (e.g., country, state, or datacenter).

required_facts.description: The cited source states: There is a sense of location independence in that the customer generally has no control or knowledge over the exact location of the provided resources but may be able to specify location at a higher level of abstraction (e.g., country, state, or datacenter).

queries.q: What makes on-demand cloud self-service independent of a provider's support staff?

span.text:
A consumer can unilaterally provision computing capabilities, such as
server time and network storage, as needed automatically without requiring human
interaction with each service provider.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: A consumer can unilaterally provision computing capabilities, such as server time and network storage, as needed automatically without requiring human interaction with each service provider.

queries.q: Which parts of an IaaS deployment can a consumer control according to the NIST definition?

required_facts.description: The cited source states: The consumer does not manage or control the underlying cloud infrastructure but has control over operating systems, storage, and deployed applications; and possibly limited control of select networking components (e.g., host firewalls).

queries.q: What connects the otherwise distinct infrastructures that make up a hybrid cloud?

span.text:
Hybrid cloud. The cloud infrastructure is a composition of two or more distinct cloud
infrastructures (private, community, or public) that remain unique entities, but are bound
together by standardized or proprietary technology that enables data and application
portability (e.g., cloud bursting for load balancing between clouds).

required_facts.description: The cited source states: Hybrid cloud. The cloud infrastructure is a composition of two or more distinct cloud infrastructures (private, community, or public) that remain unique entities, but are bound together by standardized or proprietary technology that enables data and application portability (e.g., cloud bursting for load balancing between clouds).

queries.q: What distinguishes an individual log entry from a log in the 2006 NIST guide?

span.text:
A log is a record of the events occurring within an organization’s systems and networks. Logs are
composed of log entries; each entry contains information related to a specific event that has occurred
within a system or network.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: A log is a record of the events occurring within an organization’s systems and networks. Logs are composed of log entries; each entry contains information related to a specific event that has occurred within a system or network.

queries.q: Under what conditions does the logging guide say to rotate a log file?

span.text:
Log rotation is closing a log file and opening a new log file when the first file is considered to
be complete. Log rotation is typically performed according to a schedule (e.g., hourly, daily,
weekly) or when a log file reaches a certain size.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: Log rotation is closing a log file and opening a new log file when the first file is considered to be complete. Log rotation is typically performed according to a schedule (e.g., hourly, daily, weekly) or when a log file reaches a certain size.

queries.q: What must be calculated and kept securely to detect later changes to archived logs?

span.text:
Log file integrity checking involves calculating a message digest for each file and storing the
message digest securely to ensure that changes to archived logs are detected.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: Log file integrity checking involves calculating a message digest for each file and storing the message digest securely to ensure that changes to archived logs are detected.

queries.q: Which syslog message attribute is called a facility in the 2006 NIST logging guide?

span.text:
Message type, known as a facility. Examples of facilities include kernel messages, mail system
messages, authorization messages, printer messages, and audit messages.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: Message type, known as a facility. Examples of facilities include kernel messages, mail system messages, authorization messages, printer messages, and audit messages.

queries.q: What do the three tiers of a typical log management system do?

span.text:
The
first tier encompasses the hosts that generate the original log data. The second tier includes centralized
log servers, which perform consolidation and data storage. The third tier contains consoles that are used
to monitor and review log data, and optionally may also be used to manage the log servers and clients.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: The first tier encompasses the hosts that generate the original log data. The second tier includes centralized log servers, which perform consolidation and data storage. The third tier contains consoles that are used to monitor and review log data, and optionally may also be used to manage the log servers and clients.

queries.q: What balance does the monobit test expect in a random bit sequence?

The purpose of this test
is to determine whether the number of ones and zeros in a sequence are approximately the same as would
be expected for a truly random sequence.

queries.q: What does the block-frequency test become when its block size is one bit?

For block size M=1, this test degenerates to test 1, the Frequency (Monobit)
test.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: For block size M=1, this test degenerates to test 1, the Frequency (Monobit) test.

queries.q: Why does NIST's longest-run test only need to test runs of ones?

span.text:
Note that an irregularity in
the expected length of the longest run of ones implies that there is also an irregularity in the expected
length of the longest run of zeroes. Therefore, only a test for ones is necessary.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: Note that an irregularity in the expected length of the longest run of ones implies that there is also an irregularity in the expected length of the longest run of zeroes. Therefore, only a test for ones is necessary.

queries.q: What kind of dependence is the binary matrix rank test intended to reveal?

to check for linear dependence among fixed length substrings of the original sequence.

queries.q: How does Maurer's universal test use compressibility to identify a non-random sequence?

span.text:
The purpose of the test is to detect whether or not the sequence can be
significantly compressed without loss of information. A significantly compressible sequence is
considered to be non-random.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: The purpose of the test is to detect whether or not the sequence can be significantly compressed without loss of information. A significantly compressible sequence is considered to be non-random.

queries.q: How do the initialization-vector requirements differ for CBC/CFB and OFB in SP 800-38A?

span.text:
The IV need not be secret; however, for the CBC and CFB modes, the IV for any particular
execution of the encryption process must be unpredictable, and, for the OFB mode, unique IVs
must be used for each execution of the encryption process.

queries.q: Can ECB's individual block cipher calculations be performed concurrently?

span.text:
In ECB encryption and ECB decryption, multiple forward cipher functions and inverse cipher

queries.q: Does CTR decryption call the forward or inverse cipher, and how does it recover plaintext?

span.text:
In CTR decryption, the forward cipher function is invoked on each counter block, and the
resulting output blocks are exclusive-ORed with the corresponding ciphertext blocks to recover
the plaintext blocks.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: In CTR decryption, the forward cipher function is invoked on each counter block, and the resulting output blocks are exclusive-ORed with the corresponding ciphertext blocks to recover the plaintext blocks.

queries.q: How broadly must counter-block uniqueness hold when using CTR under one key?

span.text:
The specification of the CTR mode requires a unique counter block for each plaintext block that
is ever encrypted under a given key, across all messages.

required_facts.description: The cited source states: The specification of the CTR mode requires a unique counter block for each plaintext block that is ever encrypted under a given key, across all messages.

queries.q: Where do a ciphertext block's bit errors propagate in the next block of CBC decryption?

required_facts.description: The cited source states: In the CBC mode, any bit positions that contain bit errors in a ciphertext block will also contain bit errors in the decryption of the succeeding ciphertext block; the other bit positions are not affected.

A bit for which an attacker has exactly a 50% probability of
success of guessing the value of the bit as either a zero or one. It
is also called an unbiased bit.

the transmitted MacTag (message receiver(s)).
